newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama economy grew 2.5 pct in 1996 - official.
newsitem.headline: Panama economy grew 2.5 pct in 1996 - official.

text.p: Panama's economy grew by 2.5 percent in 1996, compared with 1.8 percent growth the previous year, a top government official said on Tuesday.
"The growth domestic product grew by 2.5 percent in 1996, 40 percent more than growth in 1995," Planning and Economic Policy Minister Guillermo Chapman told Reuters in an interview.
The country's GDP grew to about $8.5 billion last year from $8.2 billion in 1995, Chapman said.
"This is the first time the economy has registered major growth since the early part of the decade after the U.S. invasion," he said.
Panama's economy reached an all-time high of 9.4 percent in 1991, two years after the United States military invaded the country, but growth slowed in subsequent years.

"We are finally turning around the slowing down of the economy and seeing the first signs of success of the government's national programs," most notably in the areas of privatization and trade liberalization, he said.
